data.title: Robusta coffee slumps to 2-1/2-year low, cocoa also down
data.description:
Robusta coffee futures on ICE slumped to a 2-1/2-year low on Wednesday, pressured by a strong dollar and ample supplies, while cocoa and sugar prices also fell.

COFFEE

* Robusta coffee settled down $52, or 1.7%, at $3,019 a metric ton after earlier setting a 2-1/2-year low of $2,998.

* Dealers said the flow of newly harvested beans from top robusta producer Vietnam was beginning to pick up and should accelerate further later this month and during early December.

* Coffee output in robusta grower Indonesia was projected to fall 8% in the 2026/27 season to 11.35 million 60-kg bags, the USDA said.

* Arabica coffee lost 2.1% to $2.7545 per lb.

* They noted ICE arabica stocks have increased for the last three days after hitting a 27-year low, tempering concerns slightly about short-term supply tightness.

* After markets closed, ICE said the amount of arabica coffee from Brazil waiting to be graded jumped to more than 245,000 bags, while the passing rate was good at about 70%.

COCOA

* London cocoa ​settled down £106, or 2.7%, to £3,891 per ton.

* Dealers said supplies appeared ample with exchange stocks climbing despite low port arrivals in top grower Ivory Coast.

* Exchange stocks on November 17 were at 100,610 metric tons, up from 96,980 tons a week earlier, they noted; at the same time last year, stocks totalled 35,990 tons.

* New York cocoa ​​lost 3.4% to $5,002 a ton.

* Dry weather may support cocoa harvesting in West Africa, said LSEG Research & Insights.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar ​settled down 0.13 cent, or 0.7%, at 18.04 cents per lb after earlier slumping to a seven-week low of 17.75 cents.

* Dealers noted sales by Brazilian mills in the session, as the country's currency hit the lowest level against the dollar since April 2025.

* There was some support from a diminished outlook for Brazil output. Because of that, some analysts expect a slightly wider global deficit in the 2026/27 season.

* Weak demand from China partly driven by improved domestic production remains a concern.

* China imported 390,000 metric tons of sugar in October, down 48% from the same month last year, according to data released by the General Administration of Customs on Wednesday.

* White sugar lost 0.8% at $507.10 a ton.

* India has invited fresh bids for duty-free import of 215,044 metric tons of raw sugar.

data.title: New Zealand central bank chief says inflation still elevated, recovery uneven
data.description:
By Lucy Craymer and Sneha Kumar

Inflation remains above its 2% midpoint as costly fuel and a weaker currency kept pressure on prices, while an uneven recovery limited businesses' scope to pass on costs, New Zealand's central bank Governor Anna Breman said Thursday at an Auckland Institute of Directors event.

  • Breman said geopolitical tensions and fuel prices were the principal drivers of inflation, despite recent declines in global oil prices. The cost of refining crude into petrol and diesel remained high, she said, while New Zealand's currency depreciation threatened to lift import prices.

  • Breman said data through the September quarter had shown less evidence that higher costs were spreading into broader consumer prices than policymakers expected. But October's selected price index suggested indirect effects could strengthen, she said.

  • Demand remained subdued, making it difficult for firms to raise prices, while weak wage growth and stable medium-term expectations helped. But underlying inflation measures remained elevated, she said, keeping officials alert to the possibility of more persistent price pressures.

  • The recovery was continuing but uneven, Breman said. Exporters had benefited from a lower currency and robust dairy and meat prices, while manufacturing, construction and services had shown signs of improvement, she added.

  • The Monetary Policy Committee would weigh incoming data before its next decision in coming weeks, Breman said, adding it would respond as needed to return inflation sustainably to its 2% target. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand surprised markets by holding its official cash rate at 2.75% in October, a decision that split its Monetary Policy Committee.

data.description:
Search Atlas/ Key word(s): Retail

Whisenhunt Media Opens Bookings for Las Vegas' Early 2027 Convention Season

18.11.2026 / 21:24 CET/CEST

The issuer is solely responsible for the content of this announcement.

LAS VEGAS, NV - November 18, 2026 (NEWMEDIAWIRE) - Whisenhunt Media, the Las Vegas video production and marketing company, is now booking event video coverage and experiential marketing and corporate events teams for the first quarter of 2027, one of the busiest stretches on the city's convention calendar. The company works with exhibitors, sponsors and companies hosting side events who want their time in Las Vegas to produce marketing that lasts well beyond the show floor.

The First-Quarter 2027 Calendar

  • CES 2027, January 6 to 9, Las Vegas Convention Center and other venues. Produced by the Consumer Technology Association, CES is where technology companies launch products, meet buyers and press, and compete for attention across several venues at once.
  • PPAI Expo 2027, January 11 to 14, Mandalay Bay Convention Center. The promotional products and branded merchandise industry's major trade show, with an education and Advance day on January 11 and exhibits January 12 to 14.
  • World of Concrete 2027, January 19 to 21, Las Vegas Convention Center, with education starting January 18. The commercial concrete and masonry construction industry's annual event, with indoor halls and outdoor equipment exhibits.
  • ANA Creator Marketing Conference 2027, March 1 to 3, Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas. The Association of National Advertisers' gathering for brand marketers working with creators and influencers.
  • HumanX 2027, March 7 to 10, Mandalay Bay. An AI conference built for business leaders, founders and investors deciding how AI changes their companies.
  • The HFA Show 2027, March 10 to 12, Mandalay Bay. The Health and Fitness Association's show for gym, club and fitness industry operators and suppliers.
  • Shoptalk Spring 2027, March 22 to 24, Mandalay Bay. A retail and e-commerce conference where retailers, brands and technology providers meet.

Dates are as published by each organizer and may change. Whisenhunt Media is an independent production company and is not affiliated with these events or their organizers.

Why a Show Needs a Content Plan

A company can spend months planning a booth, a keynote or a client reception, and the moment it ends, most of that value is gone unless it was captured with a plan. The demonstrations, customer conversations and product reveals that happen on a show floor are some of the most credible marketing a company will ever have, but only if they are filmed well and edited for the places buyers will see them.

Whisenhunt Media treats each event as the start of a content library. One well-produced event can supply months of social posts, sales collateral, email campaigns, website video and recruiting material.

How the Work Runs

  • Pre-production planning: a strategy session reviews the schedule, picks the priority sessions and moments, confirms venue logistics, and maps camera positions, audio and crew. Every deliverable is defined before a camera is packed.
  • Multi-camera crews: dedicated operators on each angle, sized to the event, so no key moment depends on one person.
  • Live direction: a producer makes real-time calls for unscripted moments and coordinates with event staff.
  • Clean audio: lav mics, podium feeds and room mics, because poor audio cannot be fixed afterward.
  • Post-production: highlight films, full session edits, executive and customer interviews and social clips, with color grading, audio mixing and branded graphics included.

More Than Coverage

For brands that want to host their own experience during a major show, such as a product launch, a client dinner, a pop-up or a VIP activation, Whisenhunt Media's experiential division plans and produces the event, turns it into a content library, and runs the paid and organic campaigns that keep it working afterward. The division is led by Reagan Pfifer, Head of Experiential Marketing and Corporate Events, who brings nearly 20 years of experience across event production, channel marketing and creative direction.

Planning Ahead

Las Vegas venues, crews and hotel blocks get busy when large shows overlap, and several of these events run back to back. Companies get the most from an event when the video plan is set alongside the booth design and the speaking schedule, so the team can capture what matters and have content ready to use the week the show ends.

Companies planning for early 2027 can request a quote at whismedia.com/services/event-coverage.

About Whisenhunt Media

Whisenhunt Media is a video-first marketing and production company based in Las Vegas, Nevada. It produces corporate and commercial video, event coverage, experiential marketing and corporate events, websites, and SEO and AI visibility programs for service businesses, SaaS companies and growing brands, and travels nationally for destination events. Learn more at whismedia.com.

data.title: US judge rejects JPMorgan bid to dismiss lurid sexual harassment case
data.description:
Key points:
  • Largest US bank, executive accused Chirayu Rana of encouraging perjury
  • Judge says case should be pursued in court, not the media
  • Rana said former colleague coerced him into sex; she countersued for defamation

By Jonathan Stempel

JPMorgan Chase failed on Wednesday to win the dismissal of a sexual harassment and discrimination lawsuit by former investment banker Chirayu Rana after accusing him of persuading his sister and a friend to lie for him.

US District Judge Lewis Kaplan in Manhattan also exhorted Rana, JPMorgan and co-defendant Lorna Hajdini, a JPMorgan executive, to press their claims and defenses through the court process, lamenting how the case "has been fought in part as a public relations battle."

JPMorgan spokesperson Brian Marchiony declined to comment. Lawyers for Hajdini and Rana did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

In court papers, Rana accused Hajdini in graphic terms of sexual harassment, including by allegedly coercing him into sex and demanding submissiveness to advance his career. He also accused JPMorgan of destroying his career by tolerating sexual coercion and racism, such as by doing nothing when colleagues called him "brown boy." Rana is of Nepalese descent.

JPMorgan and Hajdini have denied Rana's claims, and Hajdini countersued him for defamation.

In seeking a dismissal, the largest US bank accused Rana of pressing his sister Chandani Rana and friend Allan Flott to lie about seeing some of Hajdini's alleged misconduct, including when she allegedly said "I own" Chirayu Rana. Chandani Rana later recanted her testimony.

Kaplan, a federal judge for 32 years and known for his no-nonsense handling of cases, said that "once the PR appeal of media attention is put to one side," he had no way to know whether Chandani Rana's original testimony or recantation was truthful.

He said such questions "normally are better put to juries than being made into subjects for time consuming and distracting mini-trials before judges on sanctions motions." Kaplan said the parties should focus on preparing for trial, or convincing him of their cases' merits.

The judge also said the case reminded him of the 1957 Oscar-nominated movie "Witness for the Prosecution," where a barrister played by Charles Laughton cross-examines a murder suspect's wife played by Marlene Dietrich: "The question is, Frau Helm, were you lying then, are you lying now, or are you not in fact a chronic and habitual LIAR?" ["Liar" is shouted.]

data.title: Treasury, German Yields Fall Despite Hawkish Fed Expectations — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Emese Bartha and Paulo Trevisani

Treasury yields slipped even as policymakers touted the possibility of a fast increase in U.S. interest rates.

Minutes of the latest Federal Reserve rate-setting meeting, in which the U.S. central bank held borrowing costs unchanged, indicated that some policymakers are leaning toward a larger-than-usual increase by half a percentage point in December.

The minutes followed renewed comments by Fed Governor Christopher Waller supporting the supersized move as inflation drifts away from their 2% target.

"The Fed appears firmly committed to additional tightening, with the debate shifting from whether to raise rates to how dramatically," said Jeffrey Roach, chief economist for LPL Financial, in a note.

Roach, however, expects inflation to improve in November and December, leading the FOMC to stick to the usual quarter-point hike. "That said, monetary policy will likely tighten further in Q1 next year," he said.

Meanwhile, volatility in equity markets driven by AI jitters supported demand for bonds, weighing on yields. The Treasury auctioned $16 billion in 20-year bonds with indirect bidders, a group that includes foreign buyers, taking more than 60% of the offer.

Money markets currently price in a 92% probability of a 25 basis-point rate increase at the Fed's next policy meeting on Dec. 9, and assign just 8% odds to a 50 basis-point hike, according to LSEG.

"The longer the stock market slide endures, the likelier that a 50bp hike in the fed funds rate target will be completely off the table," Thierry Wizman, global FX and rates strategist at Macquarie Group, said in a note.

Financial conditions, after all, have generally tightened since before the U.S. midterm elections earlier this month, as expectations built around Democratic Party gains for federal- and state-level legislatures and executives, he said.

"Notwithstanding the hawkish overtone to market sentiment, the veil of caution created by geopolitical and macro uncertainties is helping to maintain a bid for U.S. Treasurys," said Simon Ballard, chief economist at First Abu Dhabi Bank, in a note.

The two-year Treasury yield edged higher to 4.798% from Tuesday's settlement of 4.787%, while the 10-year yield fell to 5.066% from 5.102%, according to Tradeweb. The 10-year German Bund closed at 3.375% down 0.006 percentage point, according to LSEG.

data.title: Nvidia slides as interim CEO Kress speaks to employees, says, 'Let's move forward'
data.description:
Nvidia shares slid more than 3% on Wednesday, one day after the tech giant reported better-than-expected results and raised its guidance for fiscal 2028.

Interim CEO Collette Kress addressed employees after co-founder Jensen Huang stunningly resigned this month and said, “Let's move forward,” according to CNBC, citing a person in the room who spoke on condition of anonymity.

Kress also spoke of pay raises for employees and the need for the company to move forward following Huang's resignation, which occurred after the longtime CEO admitted to infidelity and may have been the subject of a foreign intelligence operation. Nvidia's newly appointed Chairman Harvey Jones, who joined Kress on Wednesday, reaffirmed this week the company will not look to rehire Huang as CEO. (On Tuesday, Huang made his first public comments after his resignation and intimated he would be honored to return as CEO if the board of directors asked him to do so.)

Other topics that were brought up at the meeting included the search for Nvidia's next CEO, the news outlet added, citing the attendee. Kress and Jones were joined by other members of Nvidia's executive team, including Ian Buck, Jeff Fisher, Jonah Allen, Debora Shoquist, and co-founder Chris Malachowsky, the news outlet added.

Buck made his first appearance on Nvidia's conference call with Wall Street analysts on Tuesday.

The attendee added that the sentiment in the room was that some employees want Huang to return as CEO, echoing some statements from investors. On Wednesday, hedge fund manager Bill Ackman said the company's board “is not acting in the best interest of shareholders nor in a manner consistent with their fiduciary duties.”

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Seeking Alpha.

data.title: Old National Promotes Former Bremer Executive Brent Iserman to Twin Cities Regional President
data.description:
New role will connect business lines, accelerate growth, and strengthen client relationships across the Twin Cities

Brent Iserman

MINNEAPOLIS and ST. PAUL, Minn., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Old National Bank ("Old National") today announced the promotion of Brent Iserman to Executive Vice President, Twin Cities Regional President. In this newly created leadership role, Iserman will help drive growth across the Twin Cities while supporting strategic collaboration throughout the region.

As Twin Cities Regional President, Iserman will work closely with business line and regional leaders throughout Old National to align capabilities, identify opportunities for growth, and help clients benefit from the full breadth of the bank's expertise. He will serve as a connector across Commercial Banking, Wealth Management, Community Banking, Treasury Solutions & Payments, and other key business lines to deliver a coordinated approach to serving clients and communities.

In addition to leading market growth initiatives, Iserman will cultivate relationships with business and community leaders, elevate Old National's presence throughout the Twin Cities, and support collaboration across markets.

“Brent brings the market knowledge, leadership experience, and relationship-focused approach needed to help us realize the full potential of the Twin Cities,” said Tim Burke, President and Chief Operating Officer of Old National. “He has a proven ability to bring people, ideas, and capabilities together in ways that support clients, strengthen teams, and achieve results.”

Iserman joined Old National in 2025 through the bank’s partnership with Bremer Bank. He most recently served as Executive Vice President, Commercial Banking Senior Director. Throughout his banking career, Iserman has held leadership positions spanning commercial banking, market leadership, strategic planning, talent development, financial management, business development, and organizational growth. His extensive industry and enterprise experience includes leadership roles throughout the Twin Cities and across Minnesota, giving him a unique understanding of both metropolitan and community markets, and positioning him well to help advance Old National's long-term growth strategy throughout the region.

Prior to joining Old National, Iserman served in several senior leadership roles at Bremer Bank, where he helped guide business strategy, support market growth, and develop teams across the organization.

ABOUT OLD NATIONAL

Old National Bancorp is the holding company of Old National Bank. As the sixth largest commercial bank headquartered in the Midwest, Old National proudly serves clients primarily in the Midwest and Southeast. With approximately $74 billion of assets and $41 billion of assets under management, Old National ranks among the top 25 banking companies headquartered in the United States. Tracing our roots to 1834, Old National focuses on building long-term, highly valued partnerships with clients while also strengthening and supporting the communities we serve. In addition to providing extensive services in consumer and commercial banking, Old National offers comprehensive wealth management and capital markets services. For more information and financial data, please visit Investor Relations at oldnational.com. In 2026, Points of Light named Old National to “The Civic 50” for the third consecutive year – an honor recognizing the 50 most community-minded companies in the United States – and also named Old National the Financials Sector Leader among nominated banks and financial services organizations.

data.title: LIFE & BANC SPLIT CORP. ANNOUNCES PREFERRED SHARE OFFERING
data.description:
/NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION TO U.S. NEWSWIRE SERVICES OR FOR DISSEMINATION IN THE UNITED STATES./

TORONTO, Nov. 18, 2026 /CNW/ -- () (.PR.A) Life & Banc Split Corp. (the "Fund") is pleased to announce it is undertaking a treasury offering of preferred shares ("Preferred Shares") (the "Offering").

The sales period for this offering is expected to end on Thursday November 19, 2026.  The offering is expected to close on or about November 26, 2026 and is subject to certain closing conditions including approval by the Toronto Stock Exchange ("TSX").

The Preferred Shares will be offered at a price of $10.60 per Preferred Share to yield 6.8%.(1) The closing price on the TSX for the Preferred Shares on November 17, 2026 was $10.61. The offering is being led by RBC Capital Markets.

The investment objectives for the Preferred Shares are to provide holders with fixed cumulative preferential quarterly cash distributions, in the amount of $0.18125 per Preferred Share (7.25% per annum on the original $10.00 issue price), and to return the original issue price to holders of Preferred Shares on October 30, 2028.

The Fund has declared aggregate dividends on the Preferred Shares of $10.91 per Preferred Share, representing 80 consecutive quarterly dividends since inception on October 17, 2006 to October 31, 2026.  Purchasers of Preferred Shares in this Offering will be eligible to receive the full December 2026 quarterly dividend of $0.18125 per Preferred Share when the dividend is declared.

Based on the most recently calculated net asset value per unit of the Fund on November 12, 2026, the Preferred Shares have downside protection from a decline in the value of the Fund's portfolio of approximately 56%. The Preferred Shares are rated Pfd-3 by Morningstar DBRS.

The Fund invests on an approximately equally weighted basis, in a portfolio (the "Portfolio") consisting of common shares of the six largest Canadian banks and the four major publicly traded Canadian life insurance companies:

Bank of Montreal

Great-West Lifeco Inc.

data.title: Latam FX, stocks fall on stronger dollar, weaker commodity prices
data.description:
Key points:
  • LatAm stocks hit lowest since last December
  • Mexico's President says "very good meeting" with US
  • Brazil's real hits April 2025 lows vs dollar
  • Chile's peso briefly falls to a 22-month low

By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Shashwat Chauhan

Most Latin American currencies slipped against a firmer dollar on Wednesday as traders continued to bet on future Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, while weaker commodity prices added to the gloom.

The dollar firmed globally after Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank should be more aggressive in its response to inflation and either approve a half-point rate hike in December or signal a faster pace of hikes in 2027.

The dollar's global strength led to widespread losses in Latin American currencies.

Mexico's peso depreciated around 2.49%, and was on track to mark its steepest one-day drop since April 2025, after rising for the last three sessions.

Meanwhile, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said she had a "very good meeting" with her US counterpart Donald Trump as the two countries pursue negotiations to ease trade tensions.

Brazil's real was last down 1.63%, trading around its lowest level since April 2025. The country's central bank sold $1 billion in spot dollar auctions with an agreement to repurchase them later.

Investors were also awaiting the results of a vote on President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's fiscal bill amendments in the Brazilian Senate later in the day.

Latin American assets were under further pressure due to receding prices of commodities like gold and copper, given the export-oriented nature of some of the biggest economies in the region.

Copper producer Chile's peso slipped 1.61%, to its weakest level since January 2025.

Chile's economy contracted 1.8% in the third quarter from the previous three-month period, central bank data showed on Wednesday, undershooting market estimates and marking its biggest decline in six years.

"Our sense is that this GDP release, alongside the soft October inflation print and the recent fall in oil prices, keeps the balance tilted towards a rate hold at 4.50% next month," said William Jackson, chief emerging markets economist at Capital Economics.

MSCI's broad currency gauge (.MILA00000CUS) fell 1.35% to a 10-month low, while the benchmark tracking regional stocks (.MILA00000PUS) dropped 2.97% to its lowest level since December 2025.

Brazil's Bovespa eased 1.35% following losses in commodities-related firms Vale and Petrobras . The Mexican benchmark was down for the fourth straight day after hitting record highs last week.

Chilean company SQM dropped 6% after the world's second-largest lithium producer reported third-quarter results.

Latin American equities are commonly seen as a refuge from AI-related volatility because of their light exposure to technology stocks, but were under pressure on Wednesday due to their large exposure to the commodities market.

The AI trade was back in focus after chip giant Nvidia forecast quarterly revenue above Wall Street estimates late on Tuesday.

Panama was also in focus after Moody's Ratings revised the outlook on its "Baa3" sovereign credit rating to "stable" from "negative", ending an effective two-year wait-and-see period during which it retained a "negative" outlook. The rating, however, remains on the last rung of the "investment grade" category.

The country's 2032 maturity dollar bond (US698299BN37=TE) was last up 0.2 cents on the dollar, according to Tradeweb data.

data.title: AM Best Assigns Issue Credit Rating to Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited Senior Unsecured Notes
data.description:
AM Best has assigned a Long-Term Issue Credit Rating of “a-” (Excellent) to the CAD 300 million ($210 million) 5.65% senior unsecured notes due Nov. 10, 2056, and the CAD 350 million ($245 million) 5.00% senior unsecured notes due Jan. 15, 2037, by Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited (Fairfax) (Toronto, Canada) []. The outlook assigned to these Credit Ratings (ratings) is stable.

The Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating of Fairfax, as well as the ratings of its operating subsidiaries and all other debt issuances, are unchanged, as Fairfax’s adjusted debt to tangible capital, as measured by AM Best, increased marginally to 31.3% from 30.4% since Fairfax’s last debt issue, remaining within AM Best’s neutral assessment level under its Holding Company Financial Assessment. Equity credit for hybrid securities was applied to the debt leverage calculation and will be applied to Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR), as the analysis is done at the consolidated level and considers Fairfax as an insurance holding company downstreaming its resources to its operating companies. Interest coverage measured by earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) to interest expense plus preferred dividends is still expected to remain between 6.0x and 7.0x at the end of 2026, compared with 5.3x at the end of 2025, as measured by AM Best, reflecting an adequate interest coverage. Additionally, Fairfax benefits from ample liquidity and financial flexibility provided by its access to capital markets. Over 70.0% of Fairfax’s consolidated $73.0 billion investment portfolio was allocated to cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments and bonds, with a total effective duration under 2.5 years at the end of 2025. Over 65% of Fairfax’s bonds portfolio is rated highly by other agencies. Fairfax intends to use the net proceeds from the offering for general corporate purposes.

data.title: U.S. aircraft carrier leaves Middle East after reinforcements arrive
data.description:
The USS George Washington carrier strike group departed the Persian Gulf region and may be returning to Yokosuka, Japan, Bloomberg News reported Wednesday, citing two U.S. officials who requested anonymity. It was one of three American carrier groups deployed to support the naval blockade against Iran.

For investors, the departure changes the military posture around a region critical to global energy supplies. It does not by itself establish that tensions are easing: the arrival of another carrier preserves US military options, leaving uncertainty over renewed fighting and potential disruption to shipping.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt strike group arrived Monday, expanding President Donald Trump’s options should he resume active hostilities against Iran. U.S. Central Command published an image Wednesday showing the Roosevelt and George Washington sailing together.

The George Washington reached the region in August, leaving the western Pacific without a U.S. aircraft carrier. Analysts had warned that China might seek to exploit that absence.

Before this year’s Iran operations, the United States last deployed three carrier strike groups to the Middle East during the opening phase of the Iraq invasion in 2003.

data.title: Wheat Leads Selloff in Grains — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Anthony Harrup

  • Wheat for December delivery fell 4.2% Wednesday on the Chicago Board of Trade to $5.70 a bushel, leading the market lower amid broad commodities selling.
  • Corn for December delivery fell 2.5% to $4.35 1/2 a bushel.
  • Soybeans for January delivery settled down 0.7% at 12.16 3/4 a bushel.

HIGHLIGHTS

Missing Catalysts: Grain futures are down and can't find reasons to rally. "We continue to look for something to grab hold of that will still be discussed tomorrow, but it's difficult to find it," Gary Sandlund of Futures International said in a note.

Overall commodity sentiment is in a state of deflation, he said, noting big drops in oil and gold "just to name a few." Geopolitical tensions seem to be the "new normal" and markets have adapted to it, Sandlund added.

Export Worries: The market is still wondering whether China will agree to buy U.S. corn when Presidents Trump and Xi Jinping meet. "Export demand remains a central focus for the corn market following its sluggish start to the marketing year," Matthew Lucas of Total Farm Marketing said in a note. "Adding to these concerns is the recent strength in the U.S. dollar index, which could further weigh on demand by making U.S. corn less competitive in the global market."

Off Track: Russia's wheat exports will likely fall to 2.7 million metric tons in November from October's 2.9 million tons as rail shipments slow, particularly to ports in Latvia and Lithuania, grains consultancy SovEcon said.

Rail shipments are among alternatives that Russia has used to export grain since Black Sea disruptions began in July. But "rail congestion and a shortage of grain railcars are slowing shipments," SovEcon said.

INSIGHT

Local Demand: Brazil's rapid ethanol expansion is providing corn growers with an alternative to export channels for surplus production, increasing competition for available corn and supporting local prices, Rabobank senior analyst Marcela Marini said in a note. Ethanol producers need continuous year-round flow of feedstock and have significant on-site storage capacity, which provides a stable outlet for corn production.

"The result is not an end to Brazil's exportable surplus, but a reduction in the volume that must be cleared through exports," Marini said. Export parity is still an important price reference, but is becoming less dominant.

Ethanol Output: U.S. ethanol stocks rose by 563,000 barrels last week to 24.9 million barrels, their highest level in two months, according to the Energy Information Administration. Production edged down to 1.126 million barrels a day from 1.13 million barrels a day the previous week, but was up from 1.091 million barrels a day a year earlier.

Production estimates among analysts surveyed by Dow Jones ranged from 1.095 million barrels a day to 1.15 million barrels a day. Inventory estimates ranged from 23.5 million barrels to 24.7 million barrels.

AHEAD

  • The USDA will release its weekly export sales report at 8:30 a.m. ET Thursday.
  • The USDA will release its monthly Cattle on Feed report at 3 p.m. ET Friday.
  • The USDA will release its weekly Grain Export Inspections report at 11 a.m. ET Monday.
  • The USDA will release its weekly Crop Progress report at 4 p.m. ET Monday.

Write to Anthony Harrup at anthony.harrup@wsj.com

data.title: Binance says it won $6.5B worldwide freezing order after hack
data.description:
Binance said it has obtained a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing injunction from the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts as it seeks to recover assets stolen in its record Oct. 29 hack.

The court orders target unidentified perpetrators of the attack and are intended to help issuers, exchanges and other partners freeze and return stolen assets, the company said in a statement shared with Cointelegraph on Wednesday.

The orders can be served via blockchain, according to M. Kendall Day of Gibson Dunn, which represents Binance. He said market participants would be notified of updates to a “living list” of 26,000 wallet addresses identified as holding stolen assets.

Binance said some businesses require formal court orders before they can release, transfer or return frozen funds. The injunction’s $6.5 billion amount is not a tally of recovered assets, and the statement did not disclose how much had so far been returned under the orders.

Binance also said it obtained orders requiring stolen assets to be handed over. Separate interim orders cover assets frozen by certain named parties against whom no wrongdoing is alleged.

The legal action follows other efforts to secure the stolen funds in the wake of the hack, the largest-ever in the crypto industry. As Cointelegraph reported on Nov. 13, the US Justice Department said it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in assets stolen from Binance. That amount was part of more than $2.7 billion frozen through government and private sector efforts, the DOJ said.

As Cointelegraph previously reported, the attackers converted stolen stablecoins into assets such as Bitcoin and Ether , which cannot be frozen, as they lack a central issuer. Blocking the stolen tokens also does not mean they’ll be returned to Binance.

Binance said last week it had since completed coverage of affected assets after committing more than $6.34 billion from its various treasury, Secure Asset Fund for Users and insurance funds. Still, replenishing customer assets is separate from recovering the stolen cryptocurrencies from the hack.

Binance pursues expansion across Asia

Separately, Binance’s Asia-Pacific head SB Seker told Reuters on Wednesday that the exchange plans to enter five Asian markets in 2027, prioritizing South and Southeast Asia. He did not name the markets and said details were expected in the first quarter.

Seker also said Binance did not need fresh capital to absorb the losses from the October hack.

data.title: U.S. 20-Year Treasury Auction Shows Stable Demand
data.description:
By Paulo Trevisani

Demand for long-term U.S. government debt held steady Wednesday at the Treasury auction of 20-year bonds.

The monthly auction sold $16 billion in bonds, with a high yield of 5.459%, matching when-issued market yields at the time.

Following the auction, the U.S. 20-year yield slipped to 5.456% from 5.469%.

The bid-to-cover ratio, a measure of investor demand, was 2.63, matching the previous six-month average.

The auction came as Treasury yields trend lower, with demand for the relatively safe asset class boosted by volatility in the equity market. Long-term yields, however, remain somewhat elevated amid expectations of interest rate increases by the Federal Reserve.

data.title: Gold drops to 14-month low as dollar, yields rise on hawkish Fed rhetoric
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gold touches its lowest level since September 2025
  • Dollar at 19-month high
  • Waller says Fed may need to step up inflation fight
  • Silver, Platinum hit lowest level since September 2025

By Vishak Mathew

Gold sank over 3% to a more-than-one-year low on Wednesday as hawkish Federal Reserve signals raised expectations of higher interest rates, boosting the dollar and Treasury yields.

Spot gold fell 3.2% to $3,726.19 per ounce by 2:30 p.m. ET (1530 GMT). It had hit its lowest level since September 2025 earlier in the session at $3,719.55 an ounce.

US gold futures settled 3.2% lower at $3,741.90.

Minutes of the Fed's October meeting showed officials saw a growing risk that they might need to intensify efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for the moment.

"Gold won't find much relief from the Fed minutes as the overwhelming majority sees further hikes, with a couple broaching a 50bps move if inflation disappoints. Fed will hike until inflation turns, but it's not an emergency. Barring a quick reversal, today's damage suggests a probe of 3350-3450 in the coming weeks," independent analyst Tai Wong said.

The minutes echoed hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller, who said the Fed needs to get more aggressive in its response to inflation, and either approve a half-point hike in December or communicate a faster pace of rate increases in 2027.

On Tuesday, Fed officials John Williams and Alberto Musalem also signalled further rate hikes may be needed to curb inflation.

"We believe the selloff reflects mounting pressure from a strengthening US dollar, rising Treasury yields and expectations of further monetary tightening," said Naeem Aslam, CIO, Zaye Capital Markets.

The dollar strengthened to a fresh 19-month high on Wednesday as hawkish commentary and recent economic data cemented expectations for an interest rate hike next month.

Markets price in a 7.3% chance of a 50-basis-point Fed hike in December, versus 5.3% before the FOMC minutes came out. (FEDWATCH)

Higher rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold.

Spot silver slipped 5% to $45.03 per ounce, after touching its lowest level since September 2025 earlier.

Platinum dropped 4.1% to $1,370.70, after also hitting its lowest since September 2025 earlier. Palladium slid 2.2% to $949.

data.title: Dollar firmer as hawkish Waller backs aggressive Fed action
data.description:
Key points:
  • Waller says Fed needs more aggressive response to inflation
  • Traders expect 25-basis-point Fed rate hike in December
  • Sterling slips to one-month low after inflation data
  • BOJ's Ueda reiterates need for further rate hikes
  • Bitcoin down 2.5%

By Saqib Iqbal Ahmed

The dollar touched a fresh 19-month high on Wednesday as hawkish commentary from influential US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller and recent economic data cemented expectations for an interest rate hike next month.

Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's refusal to offer forward guidance has made investors more reliant on economic data and commentary from other policymakers to gauge the Fed's next move.

Waller said on CNBC that if the central bank wants to get inflation down it needs to take more "aggressive action" either through a half-point increase at the December meeting, or using the post-meeting statement to set market expectations for further hikes.

Hotter-than-expected inflation data last week have left markets fully pricing a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, and seeing a small chance of a 50-bp rise, the CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed. Data on Tuesday showed US retail sales increased moderately in October, reinforcing expectations for a rate hike next month.

"The Federal Reserve seems at the moment to be very determined to hike interest rates and maybe even aggressively do so," said Juan Perez, senior director of trading at Monex USA in Washington.

"That's the belief right now that's carrying the US dollar," Perez said.

Fed officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for the moment, the minutes of their October 27-28 meeting showed on Wednesday.

"Since the inflation data will likely improve in November and December, the FOMC will hike by 25 basis points and will not likely feel the need to hike by a larger magnitude," Jeffrey Roach, Chief Economist for LPL Financial, said in a note.

"That said, monetary policy will likely tighten further in Q1 next year," Roach said.

Still, strategists did warn the dollar may need fresh catalysts to keep it strengthening.

The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose 0.3% to 103.87, its highest since April 2025.

Traders see the benchmark Fed rate rising by around 75 basis points 12 months from now to the range of 4.50% to 4.75%, the CME FedWatch Tool showed. Investors will also scrutinize commentary from New York Fed President John Williams along with Governor Michael Barr and Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari later in the day to gauge the central bank's next move.

DOLLAR STRENGTH WEIGHS ON PEERS

The dollar's rally has pushed its peers to multi-month lows.

The euro was down 0.3% at $1.09648 and briefly touched its lowest since April 2025.

Sterling lost 0.5% to a one-month low of $1.3139 after data showed underlying UK inflation stayed steady in October from the month before, dampening expectations for an imminent rate hike by the Bank of England.

The yen was about flat on the day at 159.395 after Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda reiterated the need to tighten policy further. The Japanese currency remains close to levels at which Japanese authorities intervened in July to shore up the drooping currency.

Also in focus was a trilateral meeting due on Thursday between US President Donald Trump, China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen that could involve discussions on Russia's war with Ukraine, the Iran war, as well as trade, AI and nuclear weapons.

In cryptocurrency markets, bitcoin lost 2.5% to $62,688, inching closer to the four-month low of $62,026 touched on Sunday.
